mechanism: Betamethasone causes hypokalemia through increased urinary potassium excretion via mineralocorticoid effects, which is counteracted by potassium supplementation; however, excessive potassium supplementation with corticosteroids can lead to unpredictable serum levels and hyperkalemia risk.
action: Monitor serum potassium levels regularly during betamethasone therapy; adjust potassium supplementation based on laboratory values and clinical assessment; consider potassium-sparing alternatives if prolonged corticosteroid therapy is anticipated.
